SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Energy: Heat and its resources. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At school, pick litter and put it in the bin. That cares for the environment.

Example 2: Wash your hands with soap before eating and after using the toilet.

Example 3: Name two foods you eat at home that help you grow strong.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Energy: Heat and its resources.
2. Explain Energy: Heat and its resources to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.

4. Show that you can: appreciate the different sources of heat in the community. heat at home and community different sources of heat with the fuels used (gas, electricity, charcoal, firewood, kerosene) guardians to appreciate the types of fuels used in the community and report back.
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Energy: Heat and its resources. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Energy: Heat and its resources important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Think, pair and share heat in the community. their experiences on sources of heat at home and community
2. In groups, learners to match the different sources of heat with the fuels used (gas, electricity, charcoal, firewood, kerosene)
3. Learners interact with parents or guardians to appreciate the types of fuels used in the community and report back.
